name: The Miller's Problem
description: The miller has heard scratching and smelled something rotten from his cellar for three days, and he has not been down there since it started. He says it is rats. The rats disagree: they have all moved upstairs. The guild has been hired to go down and find out what is actually there.
title: First Real Job
epilogue: The lizard is dead and the tunnel is bricked up properly this time. The miller paid in full, kept one of its teeth as proof for the neighbours, and still sends someone else down for the flour. It was the guild's first real job, and it went well.

stages.name: The Miller's Cellar
stages.flavour: The miller hands over the cellar key and stays at the top of the stairs. Halfway down, the smell gets much worse, and the back wall of the cellar has a hole in it that was not there when he bricked it up.

stages.name: Where the Rats Went
stages.flavour: The hole opens into an old flooded drainage tunnel that runs under the mill. Something large has been dragging food back along it. The rats left because they were next on the menu.

stages.name: The Thing Under the Mill
stages.flavour: At the end of the tunnel is a cave lizard the size of a cart horse, fat on the miller's grain sacks and anything that wandered in after them. It has lived down here for years. It does not want to leave.

name: The Last Clutch
description: The old hatchery at the edge of town is falling apart. Its keeper is too old to climb the coop ladder anymore, but she has kept one last clutch of eggs alive on her own. The roof is caving in, the fence is down, and the next storm will finish the job unless someone helps.
title: Keeper of the Clutch
epilogue: The hatchery has a new roof and a fence that holds, and the wolf will not be back. The keeper still checks the work most mornings and has not found anything to complain about yet. She has handed the eggs to the guild to raise.

stages.name: The Failing Coop
stages.flavour: Half the roof is already gone. The keeper will not leave the one nest that is still dry, even to eat. She does not want gold. She wants water carried and timber hauled faster than the weather can undo it.

stages.name: The Wolf at the Fence
stages.flavour: A lone wolf has been coming back every night, pushing at the same gap in the fence. It has worked out the coop is easy food, and it will keep coming until someone stops it.

name: The Crow's Warning
description: Demons came through Thornhollow and left it standing. They did not burn it or loot it. They searched it, house by house, and left. The people they bit are slowly turning into ghouls, and nobody in town knows how to stop it. The nearest alchemist good enough to try is days away.
title: Crow-Friend
epilogue: The cure worked. Everyone who was bitten stayed human, and the tavern in Thornhollow is full again. The alchemist told the guild to keep the crow, since it clearly prefers them now. It still hangs around the guildhall most days.

stages.name: Smoke Over Thornhollow
stages.flavour: Every drawer is pulled out and every floorboard pried up, but the money and silver are still there. The demons were looking for one specific thing and did not care about anything else. The bitten are getting worse by the hour.

stages.name: The Trail North
stages.flavour: A crow lands on the town gate and will not leave the guild alone. It has a message tube on its leg with Greywick's seal. It belongs to the alchemist there, and it is trained to fly home. The guild follows it north.

stages.name: Greywick's Alchemist
stages.flavour: The alchemist hears the symptoms and starts grinding spider venom before the explanation is finished. The cure exists. Making enough of it in time is the problem, and the guild works the mortar while she measures.

stages.name: The Road Back to Thornhollow
stages.flavour: Four vials of cure, wrapped in cloth and carried like eggs, on the road back to Thornhollow. Demons are still out there, and every hour on the road is an hour the bitten do not have.

name: The Harrower's Foot
description: A second village has been hit exactly like Thornhollow: searched house by house, then burned. Two attacks, the same method, weeks apart. Somebody is sending these demons out with a job to do, and they have not finished it yet.
title: Ash-Reader
epilogue: The raiding party is dead, but none of them knew who gave the orders. They only knew to search, report, and move on. Someone above them is directing all of this, and the guild still does not know who.

stages.name: The Pattern in the Ash
stages.flavour: Every house was searched before it was burned. Cellars were emptied and floorboards pulled up, and the valuables were left behind. Whatever the demons are looking for, they did not find it here either.

stages.name: What the Foot Soldiers Take
stages.flavour: These demons fight in pairs and fall back on command. They are not hungry animals. They are soldiers following orders, and they guard each other's backs like people who expect to report in afterwards.

name: A Demon General's Ledger
description: Scouts have found a column of demons marching in formation through the Reach, led by a general. Demons do not usually march, and they do not usually take orders. If the guild wants to know who is behind the village raids, this general is the best lead it has had.
title: Tally-Breaker
epilogue: The general is dead and the ledger is at IronRest. The handwriting is the general's, but one name appears over and over as the one the reports are for: the Harrower. Nobody at IronRest has heard the name before. People have started asking around.

stages.name: The General's Column
stages.flavour: The demons march in ranks and hold them across broken ground. Someone has drilled them like an army. Breaking the column is the only way to get to the general.

stages.name: The Ledger
stages.flavour: The general kept a ledger: every village searched, the date, and what was found, which in every case is nothing. Whatever they are looking for is still out there, and the list of places left to search is getting short.

name: What the Culled Become
description: Every village on the general's list has now reported the same thing: the graves are empty. The people the demons killed did not stay dead. They got up, and they walked away together. IronRest wants to know where they went.
title: Grave-Watcher
epilogue: The risen at the barrow are destroyed, but the tomb is cracked, and whatever started raising the dead in these villages is still doing it. The ledger called it the Harrower. The guild now knows two things about it: it raises the dead, and it is interested in that tomb.

stages.name: The Empty Graves
stages.flavour: Every grave in the village has been dug open from below. There are no shovel marks. There is a trail of footprints, dozens of them, all heading east toward the old barrow-ground outside town.

stages.name: The Harvest
stages.flavour: The risen dead are standing guard on the road to the barrow. They remember their own names and answer to them. They just do not stop when you tell them to, and they have to be put down one at a time.

stages.name: Something Older Stirs
stages.flavour: The barrow-ground holds the tomb of a king buried three hundred years ago. It has been quiet that whole time. Tonight the stones over his tomb are cracking, and the risen are gathered around it like a guard of honour.

name: Proving the Bastion
description: The cure for Thornhollow reached IronRest Bastion because the guild carried it there. Captain Maeryn Thorne, who runs the Bastion, has not forgotten. She has work that needs doing and not enough people she trusts to do it. If the guild proves itself, she has something bigger in mind.
title: Lord of the Keep
epilogue: Captain Thorne kept her word. The fort, now the Keep, belongs to the guild: walls, a gate, and a garrison that answers to it. The guild stopped being hired help that day. It has territory of its own to defend now, and IronRest knows exactly who to call.

stages.name: Officers of IronRest
stages.flavour: Captain Thorne does not say please and does not repeat herself. The first job is simple: hold the Bastion's outer wall for a week while her own soldiers rest, and do not make her regret it.

stages.name: Beasts on the Border
stages.flavour: Border patrols are going missing one soldier at a time. It is a demon hound, come through one of the old wounds in the world, dragging soldiers into the treeline. It has been doing this for a month.

stages.name: The Fort in the North-West
stages.flavour: Thorne's offer is plain: take back the abandoned fort in the north-west from the demons squatting in it, and it belongs to the guild. In return, IronRest gets to call on the guild when it needs help.

stages.name: The Demon Lord's Throne
stages.flavour: A demon warlord has set itself up in the fort's great hall and built a throne out of the furniture. It is the reason the demons there hold together. Kill it and the rest will scatter.

name: Granite Crossing
description: The first request from Captain Thorne since the Keep changed hands: Granite Crossing, home of the Stone Masons Guild, has gone silent for weeks. A rival guild under a man called Garrick has taken the town gate and is holding the masons' quarry for ransom.
title: Garrick's End
epilogue: Garrick is dead and his company has scattered. They followed him for the pay, not for any cause, and there is no pay anymore. The Stone Masons Guild has made sure everyone downriver knows who reopened their gate.

stages.name: The Silent Quarry
stages.flavour: Garrick's company has the town gate and has dug in for a long stay. The stonemasons still hold the streets behind it, but they are running out of food, and Garrick knows it.

stages.name: Garrick's Reckoning
stages.flavour: Garrick has set up his camp in the middle of the working quarry, where the masons can watch from the walls. He used to run a guild like this one. Now he is just a man holding a town to ransom, and he wants to see if the guild will try him.

name: The Farm at the Edge
description: There has been no word from the border farm in ten days, and the IronRest riders sent to check have not come back either. Captain Thorne wants the Keep to handle it. Her last report says one of her own officers, Captain Vayne, was stationed out there.
title: Farmwarden
epilogue: Vayne is dead and the ritual circle in the cellar has been burned out. Her deserters have been taken back to IronRest to answer for it. The farm is being worked again. Captain Thorne has started checking on her other officers more closely.

stages.name: No Word From the Farm
stages.flavour: The crops are fine. The farmhouse is not. Deserters from IronRest's own garrison have fortified it and are turning away anyone who comes up the road. They are Vayne's soldiers.

stages.name: What Vayne Was Becoming
stages.flavour: Vayne is in the cellar, halfway through a ritual to bargain with a demon for power, and she has been paying for it with the farmhands and the missing riders. The ritual is not finished. It has to be stopped before it is.

name: The Pale Rider
description: The Paladins of the Ashen Hand have come to the Keep asking for help, which they clearly hate doing. A rider in pale armour has been killing their people on the road to Saint Aurlias' Rest, an old church they protect. They have lost three fights to him. They know who he is: their own former Lord-Commander, Ser Cael Morrow, who died five years ago.
title: Ashen-Sworn
epilogue: Ser Cael is down and buried again, this time under the church floor with the paladins standing guard over him. The Ashen Hand will not talk about the fight. They do now count the guild as allies, and they have started sending their own reports on the risen dead to the Keep.

stages.name: The Ashen Hand's Plea
stages.flavour: The paladins explain it once and do not want to explain it again. Ser Cael was buried with honours at Saint Aurlias' Rest. His grave is empty, and he is riding again in the same armour, against his own order.

stages.name: The Road to Saint Aurlias' Rest
stages.flavour: Eleven miles of road to the church, and one set of hoofprints the whole way, evenly spaced. He rides it every night, back and forth. He is guarding it.

stages.name: The Dead of Saint Aurlias
stages.flavour: The graveyard around the church has emptied the same way as the culled villages: dug open from below. Here, the risen dead are walking toward the church, not away from it. They are gathering around Ser Cael.

stages.name: The Rider in the Nave
stages.flavour: Ser Cael is waiting inside the church, still mounted. He was the best fighter the Ashen Hand ever had, and dying has not made him any worse at it. The same thing raising the dead in the Reach is holding him up.

name: The Dragon Hunt
description: A dragon is burning Emberfell, the northernmost holdfast in the Reach, one farmstead at a time. It comes down from the mountains, burns, and goes back up. The holdfast elders have pooled everything they have to pay the guild to end it.
title: Dragonbane
epilogue: Emberfell does not burn anymore. The dragon's hoard was enough to rebuild every farmstead it destroyed twice over, and the elders made sure every family got its share. They call it the dragon's one honest debt.

stages.name: Follow the Ash Trail
stages.flavour: The ash is cold but the ground underneath it is still warm. The dragon was here a day ago at most, and it always flies off in the same direction afterwards: north, toward the Cinder Pass.

stages.name: Question the Survivors
stages.flavour: The survivors all describe the same dragon: red-black, wings as wide as the valley, and it always attacks at dusk. It is not hunting for food. It burns the farm and leaves the cattle.

stages.name: Scale the Cinder Pass
stages.flavour: The only way up the mountain is the pass the dragon uses to come down. It is narrow and choked with ash, with no cover and no second route if anything goes wrong.

stages.name: The Dragon of Emberfell
stages.flavour: The dragon's lair is a ledge near the summit, and there is nowhere to retreat to. It has been burning Emberfell because Emberfell is built on what it considers its land. It will not be talked out of that.

name: Lost Kingdom Expedition
description: Master Orrin Hale, a collector from the capital, has found records of a kingdom called Caldra that dropped off every map centuries ago. He is paying three times the usual rate for an expedition to its ruins. He wants one thing from the royal vault, and he says a stone guardian built to protect it is still standing.
title: Kingdom-Finder
epilogue: With the vault open, the guardian stood down: that was the condition it was built to wait for. Inside was Caldra's crown, which Hale paid for and let the guild keep a share of. He got the records and the proof his family's old stories were true. Caldra is still a ruin, but it is on the maps again.

stages.name: Chart the Grey Marches
stages.flavour: Six days across empty grey moorland, following Hale's old maps, until a paved stone road appears out of nowhere. Caldra's roads were built to last, and this one has.

stages.name: Cross the Silent Bridge
stages.flavour: The bridge into Caldra is three hundred years old and still perfectly solid. Caldra's masons were very good. Its guards were too, and the gatehouse on the far side is still armed with working traps.

stages.name: Open the Sunken Vault
stages.flavour: The royal vault is sealed with stone, then steel, then old wards. The stone guardian at its centre was built to stop anyone without the king's seal. Hale's records include a drawing of the seal. It is not enough on its own, but it is a start.

name: Demon Fortress Assault
description: A demon fortress has stood in the Reach for nine years, held by a demon lord and sealed by wards nobody has broken. The Crown is finally assaulting it, and the guild has been asked to lead the breach. There will not be a second attempt.
title: Hellgate Breaker
epilogue: The demon lord is dead and the fortress has fallen. The choir did not stay to be counted. In the confusion of the final fight it pulled itself out of the walls and got away. Nobody knows where it went yet.

stages.name: Break the Outer Siege
stages.flavour: Ladders on the walls, fire in the ditch, and a long night of fighting to reach the main gate. This is the easy part, and it still costs plenty.

stages.name: Break the Warding Choir
stages.flavour: The fortress wards are powered by a choir: a demonic construct of many mouths that sings the wards in place. It does not have to be destroyed, only interrupted long enough for the gate to come down.

stages.name: The Iron Gate
stages.flavour: The gate is held by the demon lord's personal guard. They held it through the last siege nine years ago and have been preparing for this one ever since.

stages.name: Descend to the Throne
stages.flavour: The throne room door is already open. The demon lord is waiting inside, and it knows the fortress is lost. It intends to take as many of the guild with it as it can.

name: Search for the Ancient Crown
description: Lady Seren Ashcombe claims descent from the old coastal kings, and to prove it she needs their crown, which was broken into three pieces and hidden when the line ended. She has tracked down all three. One is in a fen, one is in a banker's vault, and one is in a smith's forge. She is paying the guild to collect them.
title: Crownbearer
epilogue: Lady Ashcombe has her crown, reforged in one piece, and is pressing her claim in the capital. Whether the court accepts it is her problem. She paid in full and threw in a ring from the old royal collection for the trouble.

stages.name: The Fragment in the Fen
stages.flavour: Knee-deep in cold water, an old suit of enchanted armour stands guard over the first fragment. There is nobody inside it. It was set there to guard the piece and it is still doing its job.

stages.name: The Fragment in the Vault
stages.flavour: The banker insists the second fragment is just a paperweight and will not sell it. He knows exactly what it is worth, and he has hired guards to prove it. The guild will have to take it quietly.

stages.name: The Fragment in the Fire
stages.flavour: The last fragment was hidden inside a working forge, sitting in coals hot enough to melt steel. The smith who owns it does not know it is there. Getting it out without wrecking the forge, or the smith, is the job.

name: The Goblin King's Warband
description: Three goblin warbands used to raid separately and get in each other's way. A chieftain named Grukk has beaten each of their leaders in single combat and taken their cleavers, and now all three follow him. One horde is a much bigger problem than three small ones.
title: Warband-Breaker
epilogue: Grukk is dead, and without him the horde has split back into three warbands squabbling over the hills. His three cleavers hang in IronRest now, a reminder of how close the goblins came to being a real army.

stages.name: Scatter the Outriders
stages.flavour: Grukk's outriders are loud and careless: clattering armour, torches lit before dark, boasting about the next raid. Cut them down before they get back to camp, and Grukk will not see the guild coming.

stages.name: The Chieftain's Camp
stages.flavour: Grukk carries all three cleavers strapped across his back. The horde follows him because he won every fight, and he made sure they were all watching. He has never fought anyone bigger than a goblin.

name: The Gathering Horde
description: Grukk's horde fell apart when he died, but one of his lieutenants, Skarn, saw how Grukk did it and is trying to do it again. He is calling the warbands back together with the same offer: follow whoever wins every fight. If he finishes, IronRest will face the same horde again, led by someone who watched how the last one fell.
title: Horde-Breaker
epilogue: Skarn is dead before his horde was finished, and the warbands have gone back to fighting each other. IronRest expects another goblin to try this one day. For now, there is no horde.

stages.name: Scattered, Not Gone
stages.flavour: The warbands should be raiding each other by now. Instead, goblin messengers are running between the camps, all carrying the same offer from Skarn. Some of the warlords are already listening.

stages.name: The New Court
stages.flavour: Skarn has set up in the ruins of Grukk's old camp and is collecting cleavers from every goblin who challenges him and loses. He is copying Grukk exactly, because he knows it worked.

stages.name: Snuff the Ember
stages.flavour: Skarn has half the warbands already. Stopping him now is a hard fight. Stopping him in a season, when he has all of them, would be a war.

name: The Hollow Choir
description: The choir that powered the demon fortress's wards got away when the fortress fell. It has turned up again in an old cathedral in the Reach, rooted itself into the building, and started singing new wards around it. Nobody who has gone in to look has come back out.
title: Choir-Silencer
epilogue: The choir is dead this time, torn out of the rafters and burned on the cathedral floor. Its wards went with it. The cathedral has been reconsecrated and the bells ring again. Most people have stopped flinching when they do.

stages.name: Follow the Hymn
stages.flavour: The singing carries for miles and never stops for breath. The wards woven into it are the same ones the guild broke at the fortress. The choir is making the cathedral its new fortress.

stages.name: The Choir Loft
stages.flavour: There are no singers in the loft. The choir is a single demonic creature fused into the rafters, dozens of mouths taking turns so the note never stops. It is what kept the fortress sealed for nine years.

stages.name: Silence the Chord
stages.flavour: The choir is close to finishing its new wards. Once they are done, the cathedral will be as hard to break as the fortress was. It has to be stopped while it is still building them.

name: The World-Ender's Vigil
description: Every culture with written records describes the same thing: something at the edge of the world that ends places, slowly, from the outside in. It has no name that any two of them agree on. A patron has funded five expeditions to find it, and none came back. He has now asked the guild, because he no longer wants to send strangers. Five stages, and no easy ones.
title: World's End
epilogue: The thing at the edge of the world is dead. It never had a name, and it still does not. The Vigil can rest now, and the road has gone back to being hillside. The patron has stopped funding expeditions.

stages.name: The Road That Should Not Exist
stages.flavour: Three nights ago, a road appeared in the hills that was not there before. By morning, mapmakers in three towns had drawn it onto their maps without speaking to each other, each sure they had always known it was there. The patron says this is how it starts: the world rearranges itself around the thing, and the road leads to it.

stages.name: The Watchers in the Dark Between Stars
stages.flavour: Past the treeline, the stars overhead are ones nobody has charted. Six tall, thin figures stand at the end of the road, keeping a count of something. They do not serve the thing at the end of the road. If anything, it answers to them, and it is not the only thing they are counting. They let the guild pass.

stages.name: The Court of the Unmade King
stages.flavour: Beyond the Watchers is a hall full of broken crowns, ruled by a demon that calls itself a king. It feeds on the wreckage the thing at the end of the road leaves behind, and it does not want anyone getting close enough to stop the feeding.

stages.name: The Breaking of the Vigil
stages.flavour: Below the hall is a wall of pale light, held up by worn-out beings who have been holding back the rot since before anyone kept records. The wall is failing. The guild has to help hold it long enough to reach the other side.

stages.name: The World-Ender
stages.flavour: On the other side of the wall is the thing itself: a shape that barely holds together, and is slowly eating the world from the edges inward. This is what the five expeditions found, and none of them survived it.

name: The Last Pilgrimage
description: Travellers on an old pilgrim road have been disappearing near an abandoned shrine and coming back days later, unharmed but shaken. They all say the same thing: something at the shrine made them kneel and walked them through a funeral rite, their own, even though they were not dying. The shrine belongs to a god of death nobody has worshipped in centuries.
title: Pilgrim's Herald
epilogue: The guild now knows what is at the end of the road: the Last God, the god of the final mile, starving because nobody walks to it anymore. It is still down there, still trying to do its job for people who stopped coming centuries ago.

stages.name: The Waystone
stages.flavour: The shrine marks the start of the old pilgrim road. Whatever is here is not a monster. It is the god's last remaining power, still trying to perform the rite it was built for on anyone who walks past. It does not fight. It insists.

stages.name: The Scribes' Silence
stages.flavour: Behind the shrine is the archive of the order that kept the pilgrimage records. It was locked up when the last scribe died and has not been opened since. The records inside should explain what happened.

stages.name: What the Archive Remembers
stages.flavour: The records are half rotted, but the story is clear enough. Pilgrims used to walk this road in their last days, and the god walked them peacefully into death. Over a century, fewer and fewer came, until none did. The god was never abandoned on purpose. People just forgot.

stages.name: The Road That Still Opens
stages.flavour: Under the archive is the real pilgrim road. It opens for one reason only: someone willing to walk it in place of the pilgrims who never came. The guild did not come here to do that. The road has opened anyway.

name: The Hollow King's Return
description: For guilds a run or two into prestige. The barrow-ground east of the culled villages has finally broken open. King Haldren, buried there three hundred years ago, has risen, and his dead court has risen with him. He is marching back toward the capital he once ruled, to take his crown again.
title: Kingslayer Twice Over
epilogue: Haldren is buried again, under far more stone than last time, and his court with him. The magic that raised them died when he did. The barrow-ground is quiet, and IronRest has posted a permanent watch on it anyway.

stages.name: The Grave Reopens
stages.flavour: The tomb seal held for three hundred years and gave way last night. Haldren's guards came out first, and they are holding the barrow while the rest of his court climbs out.

stages.name: The Procession of the Dead Court
stages.flavour: Every advisor Haldren had executed in life walks behind him now, perfectly obedient. They never obeyed him this well while they were alive. They have to be cut down before the procession reaches the road.

stages.name: The Bridge of Forgotten Oaths
stages.flavour: Haldren's route crosses an old royal bridge enchanted to collapse under anyone who has broken a sworn oath. His court crosses it easily. The guild has to cross it too.

stages.name: The Second Coronation
stages.flavour: Haldren has reached the ruins of his old throne room and put his crown back on. The kingdom forgot his name long ago. He has not forgotten it, and he will fight for it.

name: The Man Who Sells Maybe
description: A man named Grimsby has parked a card cart on the road outside town and spent the week taking people's money. Pay a coin, flip three cards, win if they match. Nobody wins. Three townsfolk have come to the guild separately, a farmer, a tavern keeper and a guard's wife, all asking for the same thing: find out how he's doing it.
title: The One He Doesn't Cheat
epilogue: The Vasse brothers left without the cart and without their money. They still want both, but collecting now means going through the guild. In return, Grimsby threw the shaved deck in the fire in front of everyone and handed over the loaded coin he'd been using for side bets. He plays a fair game now and still charges for it. He also says he owes the guild, and has promised to pay it back. Nobody has seen how yet.

stages.name: A Cart on the Old Road
stages.flavour: The cart is easy to find. Grimsby has been working the same stretch of road all week and makes no effort to hide. The guild talks to the people who lost money. The stories match: the game looks fair, the cards look fair, and Grimsby is friendly the whole time he takes your coin. He has lost exactly once all week, and the man who won was seen drinking with him later.

stages.name: The Marked Deck
stages.flavour: Someone from the guild plays a few rounds while another watches from the crowd. The trick is simple once you see it: the winning cards are shaved a hair thinner, and Grimsby can feel them as he deals. He only lets the matches land when the bet is too small to matter. He spots the watcher halfway through, finishes the hand anyway, and asks if they'd like to talk somewhere quieter.

stages.name: What Grimsby Owes
stages.flavour: Grimsby doesn't deny any of it. He borrowed the money for the cart from the Vasse brothers, two lenders out of the dock district, and the rigged game was how he planned to pay them back on time. He's late. The brothers turn up that evening to take the cart and whatever else he has. The guild is standing next to him when they do. Grimsby asks, very politely, if that could stay the case.

name: Bandits on the Old Road
description: Every caravan on the old trade road is being stopped and charged a toll at knifepoint, sometimes by a different crew each week. There are too many bandits working too well together for this to be chance. Someone is organising them.
title: Roadwarden
epilogue: Rook is dead and his crews have scattered. The road is clear again, and the caravans are paying the guild's escort rates instead of tolls. Someone will try it again eventually. That is a problem for next season.

stages.name: The Toll Nobody Asked For
stages.flavour: A merchant convoy limps into town two wagons short. The crew that robbed them was organised, patient, and polite about it. Half a dozen other convoys have the same story this month.

stages.name: Whose Colours Are These
stages.flavour: A torn banner from the ambush site belongs to no crew the guild knows. Asking around turns up three other bandit gangs flying the same colours. Someone has been recruiting them.

stages.name: The Self-Crowned King of the Old Road
stages.flavour: The recruiter is a former caravan guard called Rook, who has set himself up in a ruined watchtower and calls himself King of the Old Road. Nobody gave him the title. He has a small army of bandits who had no better offer.

name: Something Big in the Foothills
description: Herders in the foothills are losing whole flocks overnight. Fence posts are being pulled out of the ground, not broken, and the footprints in the mud are bigger than a man is tall. It is hill giants, and there is more than one.
title: Ridgebreaker
epilogue: With their leader dead, the rest of the warband scattered back up the ridge. Hill giants tend to wander off rather than come back for revenge. The herders have rebuilt their fences, and the foothills should stay quiet for a while.

stages.name: Torn Fences, Missing Herds
stages.flavour: The fence was pulled up, posts and all. The drag marks leading up into the hills are wide enough for two people to walk side by side. The flocks went that way.

stages.name: The Ridge Warband
stages.flavour: It is a hill giant warband, six of them, camped on the ridge in shelters built from stolen timber, eating their way through the herders' sheep. They will not leave while there is food.

stages.name: The Ridgebreaker
stages.flavour: The biggest of them leads the others by being the biggest. There is a boulder by the camp with a dent in it the size of a fist, and he likes to point at it when anyone argues.

name: Full Moon Over Ashvale
description: Ashvale, a hunting-lodge town, wants its wolf problem solved before the next full moon. The tracks are the wrong shape for wolves, the attacks follow the moon's phases, and a hunter who survived a bite has started acting strangely. Ashvale has werewolves, and the guild has a week.
title: Moonhunter
epilogue: The alpha is dead and the pack is broken. Ashvale is grateful, and shaken. Holt was one of their own, and the guild was the one that had to put him down. Ashvale is still working out how to mourn him.

stages.name: Not Wolves
stages.flavour: The bite marks are too wide for a wolf and every attack has landed within a day of the moon. The pack is people for most of the month. They live in or near Ashvale.

stages.name: The Turned Neighbour
stages.flavour: One of the bitten hunters, a man named Holt, stopped answering to his own name three nights ago. He has already turned, and he is with the pack now. There is no way left to bring him back.

stages.name: Under a Full Moon
stages.flavour: The pack runs under the full moon tonight. The alpha has to die before moonrise is finished, or the guild will be fighting the whole pack at full strength in the dark.

name: The Body Snatcher Problem
description: The Pell household, one of IronRest's oldest families, has started acting wrong. They say the right things but at the wrong pace, and their laughter comes a half second late. Their neighbours are worried. The watch has quietly asked the guild to look into it.
title: Unmasker
epilogue: The skinweaver is dead. The real Pells were among the bodies in its lair. The watch has opened an inquiry into how many other households it may have reached before this one, and the guild will hear the moment they find anything.

stages.name: Wrong Rhythm
stages.flavour: Every answer the Pells give is correct and sounds rehearsed, as if someone learned how a normal family talks by watching one. None of the servants have been seen in a week.

stages.name: The Grave-Robbers' Trail
stages.flavour: A disturbed grave in the Pell family crypt leads to a tunnel, and the tunnel leads to a lair full of bodies, some of them the missing servants. Something has been taking people and studying them.

stages.name: What Wears Them Now
stages.flavour: It is a skinweaver: a creature that takes a person, copies them from the inside out, and replaces them. It has replaced every Pell in the house. It is not going to let itself be found out without a fight.

name: Hunt-a-Lich
description: The risen dead in the Reach have started acting like an army: taking positions, retreating, and regrouping. Something intelligent is commanding them. IronRest wants to know who before the next attack.
title: Grave-Marked
epilogue: The guild knows where Ostrel is and what he is: a lich, in an old ossuary nobody had mapped in decades. What he is working on down there is still unknown. He has stopped hiding, which means he thinks he is nearly finished.

stages.name: The Dead Don't Usually Plan
stages.flavour: These dead hold positions, fall back when they are losing, and regroup somewhere the guild has not found. Someone is giving them orders, and is close enough to watch.

stages.name: A Name in the Dark
stages.flavour: A ritual circlet taken from one of the commanding dead carries a maker's mark: Ostrel, a necromancer IronRest hanged ninety years ago. He did not stay dead. He made himself a lich.

stages.name: The Door He Didn't Bother Locking
stages.flavour: Ostrel's ossuary is not hidden or guarded. He knows the guild is coming and he does not care. He is busy with something, and he does not plan to stop for visitors.

name: Quiet in Millbrook
description: Every report from Millbrook says the same thing: the town looks fine and sounds fine, but it is not. Everyone in town gives the same answers to questions, word for word, even people who have never met. A whole town has started agreeing on everything, and nobody there thinks it is strange.
title: Watcher of Millbrook
epilogue: The threads lead under Millbrook to something that controls the townsfolk through them. The townsfolk are not lying. They believe what it tells them. The guild has traced it as far as the tunnels under the town. It knows the guild is coming.

stages.name: Flat Answers
stages.flavour: Every resident gives the same calm answer to completely different questions, with the same pause first, as if they are listening to someone before they speak. They are. Each of them has a thin pale thread under the skin at the back of the neck.

stages.name: The Trail Goes Quiet
stages.flavour: The threads all run into the ground. When the guild starts following them, the town closes ranks: every lead goes cold at once, every resident forgets what they said the day before. Whatever is on the other end of the threads knows it is being followed.

name: The Loom Beneath
description: The thing under Millbrook has stopped hiding. Its threads are spreading to the farms around the town, and anyone who sleeps near them wakes up agreeing with everyone else. The guild is going down into the tunnels to find it.
title: Thread-Walker
epilogue: The guild calls it the Loom. It has no name for itself. They know where it is, how it controls people, and that towns further along the road are starting to report the same symptoms. Ending it means going down there and cutting it out at the root.

stages.name: Underneath
stages.flavour: The tunnels under Millbrook were not dug. They were grown, smooth-walled and lined with pale threads, all pulling toward the same point. The deeper the guild goes, the thicker they get.

stages.name: One Voice, Too Many Mouths
stages.flavour: At the centre is a vast growth, part fungus and part something else, with threads running into every person in Millbrook. It speaks through all of them at once, calmly asking why anyone would want to undo the first time the whole town has ever agreed.

name: The First Haul
description: Old Bram, a retired quartermaster, corners the guild before its first job is even finished. Buying every scrap of ore and timber from the shop is money a guild should keep for itself, he says. The old gathering grounds outside town are still there. Someone just has to clear them.
title: Provisioner
epilogue: Bram has taught the guild everything he knows about getting ore, timber, herbs and fish out of the land around IronRest. The rest is practice. The supply room is filling up, and the guild is spending a lot less at the shop.

stages.name: Clearing the Old Grounds
stages.flavour: The gathering grounds have not been used in years. Brambles cover the quarry, the woodyard is overgrown, and the herb garden is all weeds. None of it is dangerous. All of it needs clearing.

stages.name: A Lesson in the Old Ways
stages.flavour: Bram walks the guild round every node himself: when to strike, when to wait, and which glints are worth running for. Forty years of never paying for a nail, and he is happy to share all of it.

name: The Kindred Moon
description: A letter reaches the guild from Ashvale, addressed by name and marked private. It is from Edric Marsh, a hunter who survived the werewolf pack the guild broke there. He survived the bite too, and he has been hiding what that means ever since. The next full moon is days away, and he is asking for help before it comes.
title: Kindred
epilogue: It worked, in a way. Edric is still himself, with his own memories and his own mind, but the shape he takes at the full moon is now permanent and under his control. Ashvale knows now and has not decided how it feels. The guild has already decided.

stages.name: A Name From Ashvale
stages.flavour: Edric asks for privacy first and help second. The bite never fully healed, and every full moon he has to lock himself in a cellar. Ashvale does not know, and he would like to keep it that way.

stages.name: What the Hedge-Witch Wants
stages.flavour: An old hedge-witch near Ashvale knows a rite that might work. Her price is a moonsilver bloom that only grows on a ridge full of wolves, and it has to be picked during the full moon week. She is sympathetic. She is not doing it for free.

stages.name: The Rite at Ashvale
stages.flavour: The circle only has to hold until the moon has fully risen. It does not. Edric starts to turn halfway through, and the rite draws something else in with him: a wild spirit drawn by the magic, which tries to take him over.

stages.name: What Walked Out of the Circle
stages.flavour: When the moon is up, something is standing where Edric was, and for a long moment nobody, Edric included, knows how much of him is left. Then he says the guild's name, correctly, and asks if it worked.
